SO LONG ELLIS PARK

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Inner City Decay at a point of no return or is there still a gap to revive an area rich with history and iconic sights that are over run by crime and grime.

Unique Selling Point:
** ALLOWS US TO TELL A BIGGER PICTURE STORY OFF THE BACK OF A SPORTS STORY
** A LOOK AT THE GAS PIPELINE EXPLOSION IN A LESS OBVIOUS WAY

Summary:
The Springboks’ final game on home ground raised questions about the future of the iconic Ellis Park Stadium – has it reached its sell-by date with Joburg CBD’s urban decay keeping spectators away?

It allows us to have a look at the current state of the inner city – how did we get here, and what is the future for an area once the epicenter of business and play.

We hit the streets, speak to some key players and address the challenges plaguing downtown Joburg.


Further information:
We take a look at the history of Ellis Park and where it finds itself in 2023 – an epic stadium now plagued by inner city decay. We ask what the future holds for sporting events and businesses in the area that seems to be losing the battle to regenerate the Joburg CBD.

**CAPACITY AT EVENTS – DROPPED.
Over the last year there’s been a significant drop in attendance at sporting events held at Ellis Park – some have sighted the fall of the city and the security risks around the stadium. Speaking to Ken Borland from the Citizen – he agrees the area is not what it used to be but pointed out that there were factors to consider around the Springbok vs Agentine game – 1. Just two weeks earlier there was the Wallaby game at Loftus – a bigger competitor for the Boks from a spectator perspective and it was two big matches in GP in a short time and international tickets are cheap. 2. The weather – it was COLD in Jozi that Saturday.

**ALTERNATIVE PROPERTY PERSPECTIVE
The inner city may be in a shocking state for middle-class South Africans, but for foreigners and locals from rural communities downtown JHB is a step up, as sad as that may be – it is seen as a stepping stone to a better life for many who come from informal settlements and find a space in a big city to pursue jobs and a future for their families.

**PROPERTY INTERVIEW
TUHF is a specialised commercial property financing company that finances property investors exclusively in inner cities. This company has unique hands on insight into the challenges investors face when it comes to regenerating inner cities – they speak to the vision, the struggles with lack of service delivery and a surge in criminal activity. While there is interest from investors, and there has been some success to turn inner city precincts around (usually without government assistance) – it’s become increasingly challenging to keep their strategies going as Joburg seems to be crumbling. Many investors are now looking outside of downtown JHB to areas where there is more potential from privately managed services and less reliance on government.



INTERVIEWS

 THE STADIUM – Ellis Park Managing Director, Pieter Burger – we’ll film at the stadium. Do a walk through the museum, interview inside and maybe a bit outside on the streets around the stadium.
 RUGBY LEGEND – TBC – I’m trying John Smit. Will hopefully know today. Otherwise, Ken Borland from the Citizen. The idea is to get a perspective from someone that has a special connection to the stadium but also sees the current state of the city as an issue – John Smit is also part of SSG, a security group.
 LOCAL SECURITY – Hendrik de Klerk from Bad Boyz Security – we’ll film this late afternoon on our first shoot day, to get the rush hour effect, and to see the vibe change as the sun sets. We’ll also get visuals around the pipeline blast scene and get some links there.
 BREACON OF HOPE - TROYVILLE HOTEL – they share their journey to keep their spot a must-visit location – what it takes to run a successful business in downtown Jozi and why they are still hopeful about the area.
 INNER CITY PROPERTY GURU – Sivan Govender, Operations Director at TUHF

** I’m purposely avoiding the Municipality – they don’t know their arse from their elbow and the mayor keeps changing, and they bicker – the reality is it’s shitshow, they’re not doing anything and they’re just going to give us a bullshit take on it.

TREATMENT
 FILMING STYLE – I’m going to try and do a lot of it looser – outside, walk and talk, show and tell. Some will be in doors of course, but it’s a story about the city – I think we need to be in the city.
 EDIT IDEAS – We won’t have vox pops with spectators – but will have some tweets and comments from Social Media so I’m thinking to build something device to bring up some of the comments. Working on a intro concept for the elements.

FINAL SCRIPT: SO LONG ELLIS PARK - 11 minutes

OPENING VISUAL SEQUENCE
Shots of stadium exterior… with music…
AUDIO - bleed in crowd noise…
AUDIO - bleed in upsound from 1995 Final … yada yada STRANSKEEEEEEEE
SHOW THE WIN ON THE FIELD // FINAL WHISTLE UPSOUND COMMENTATOR

UPSOUND FRANCOIS PIENAAR:“We didn't have 60,000 South Africans, we had 43 million South Africans”

VO: This scene is quite possibly one of South Africa’s most important sporting moments - it united the country and cemented Ellis Park Stadium’s place in history.

But is the curtain now coming down on this iconic stadium?

VISUALS: SOCIAL MEDIA DEVICE - +/- 15 SECONDS
1. “Awful, dangerous, inaccessible” (NICKY)
2. “It’s a very dangerous part of Joburg” (RUDI)
3. “Maybe it’s time to relocate the Ellis Park Stadium” (NAN)
4. “People too nervous to go” (MIAS)
5. “It’s pointless for Lions carry on playing there” (ARISTO)

VO: Today central Johannesburg is plagued by a lack of service delivery… overrun by crime….. and covered in grime.

And the city's landmarks haven't been spared the consequences.

AUDIO NOTE - CLEAN UP ICONIC WORD
LINK: It’s an iconic stadium set in the heart of downtown Johannesburg and home to some of South Africa's most historic moments. But could the stadium be reaching its sell by date with inner city decay creeping in?

KEN: The actual In-Stadium experience is fine. // that's in their control.

UPSOUND KEN INTRO: I’m Ken Borland - I’m a freelance Sports Journalist

KEN: where they're situated, // Jo'burg CBD basically close to Hillbrow. Um, you know what, what can they do. //The attendance has dropped down and it's just not a very pleasant place to go to - you know, that's the honest truth.

VISUAL MOMENT - OF QUICK CUTS OF THE CITY LOOKING SHIT +/- 2 seconds…

DE KLERK: The area needs intervention

AUDIO NOTE: INTRO ALLOW WALK SHOT FOR 1 SECOND BEFORE HE SPEAKS…

INTRO DE KLERK: My name is Mr. D and do security in the inner city and Hillbrow area.
DE KLERK: The feeder routes, // that sections between the freeways and ELLIS Park that gauntlets that you go through // that's where people's bodies when they get that fight or flight chemicals coming through.

VO: The areas around the stadium are in a dire state.

VISUAL MOMENT…

CLAIRE: The negative experience around coming to Ellis Park is not Ellis Park, but it's getting in and getting out of it.
DE KLERK: Totally. it’s leaving under ponte, bertrams, hillbrow going through braamfontein// the streets, the side streets. // we need proper policing of precincts like this//

VO: But for many, these areas are far more than inconvenient feeder routes to an aging stadium.

SIFISO: This is our home. // If we abandon it, who's going to look after it?

INTRO SIFISO: I’m Sifiso stayed in the city for more than a decade, now I’m a tour guide taking them around the inner city of Johannesburg.
SIFISO: I think most of the South Africans pretty much you ask them about Hillbrow for the only thing that comes into their mind It's about the crime and how unsafe it is to be in the city, you know?

VISUAL BREATH….SHORT BREATH

SIFISO: It's the hub of JHB. You know, it's one of the most densely populated neighborhoods, especially to the black community. This is the place where you can hustle or start something art, which allows everybody to dream big and to do whatever they want to be, you know?

VO: Sadly, the city's demise casts a shadow on whatever opportunities exist here

INTRO SIVAN: I’m Sivan Govender…..operations ex for TUHF limited
SIVAN: You can't invest in an environment that's deteriorating. As much as we’re committed to the inner city, // we also can't be foolish.

VO: The company provides property development finance loans. Two decades on, they’ve invested over R5 billion in the inner city - but it’s becoming increasingly difficult to sell downtown Joburg.

LINK: While there are sections in the inner city that feel promising – it’s cleaner, it’s maintained – the majority isn’t. It’s dirty, it’s derelict, infrastructure on the brink of collapse – it feels like downtown Joburg is imploding

VO: No better demonstrated than an alarming incident in mid-July.

UPSOUND (CCTV TAXI FLIP - look for clean clip)

VO: This almost apocalyptic scene is the result of an underground gas leak….. (BEAT)

Sections in the area will remain closed for months to come - adding to the city’s already long list of challenges from water supply to road infrastructure and a general lack of municipal services

SIVAN: This is a 20 year problem that's just now become too much to handle for the current coalition players.// what's happening is investors are moving away from the inner city. // they want to go to the environments that are controlled, where they have operational city improvement districts, where people pay levies to maintain the upkeep of the area.

VO: Some feel, that’s exactly what Ellis Park Stadium should be doing.

KEN: // if you look at the surrounding area around Ellis Park // is there anything going on there that makes you think, okay, things are improving, that if we just hold out, you know, there's a plan and things are going to get better? No, it doesn't look like it.

VISUAL MOMENT
VISUAL MUSIC SUNSET…..

LINK: When you leave Ellis Park after a match, you leaving in the dark and you leaving a safe cocoon and you're entering a whole other world that, frankly, is scary. It's dark, it's grimy and has seedy elements. Has anything ever happened to me in the streets leaving the stadium? No. But do I feel uncomfortable and uneasy? Absolutely.

DE KLERK: Your personal space gets smaller because you can’t see the people beyond the car. On the car. Each moment somebody is knocking on a window. We had quite a few incidents through here and it doesn't get reported the Hillbrow Police Station, the guy will drive home //he doesn't want to go to your police station because of the bad experience.
CLAIRE: I mean, we're not even that far from here. We're not even that far from Ellis Park. It's just behind us.
DE KLERK: This is a kilometer out of Ellis Park. //We have our strip clubs, quite big taverns, // and all this is aspects that's bringing the area down.

VO: It seems that's affecting the game day experience, and could be the reason for the empty seats at the July test between the Boks and Argentina

UPSOUND ETSEBETH SCORING… and Etsebeth… WHISTLE…

VO: The more than 60 thousand seat stadium was anything but full.

But, organisers were quick to point out the attendance was still a record for a game against the South Americans.

But that hasn't spared the stadium from flak

UPSOUND PIETER INTRO: Pieter Burger, Managing Director - EAP.

PIETER: crime is a national problem within southern Africa that we're faced with and we need to deal with. And we tried to manage that through various different initiatives as best we possibly can. // over a thousand safety and security officers were deployed on the day that was just private security company // over 200 300 to JMPD and also SAPS officers //

DE KLERK: The security companies does awesome jobs. JMPD are all on duty during the day, but my concern is the bigger picture. What is the city of Joburg doing to develop the area permanently?

SIFISO: look ack - ignore it all you want it’s still parf of us need to embrace it.

VO: But Small business owners are stepping up - it’s not all doom and gloom -

INTRO RAUL: Raul de Lima, proprietor and owner of The Troyville Hotel
RAUL: // it's up to us to do it,// It's about taking back and owning the city

VO: Less than a kilometer from the stadium grounds is yet another iconic Joburg Landmark. The Troyville Hotel opened its doors in 1939 - the same year the Second World War began. A lot has happened in those 85 years, and owners have come and gone.

RAUL: This is a kind of a property that sits sort of almost on the cusp of the wrong side of town, so to speak. // this building, this precinct. // It's iconic.

VO: De Lima bought the Hotel two years ago, taking over what he calls a pretty run down gem and returning it to its former glory

RAUL: what we really enjoyed was the fact that we could come here, put our money where our mouth was, invest, fix it up, create employment, // I think the community recognizes that we've invested and they respect that.

SIFISO: A lot of change that needs to happen - let’s work together and turn our city back.

VO: DE LIMA hopes his investment will draw other like-minded entrepreneurs back to areas in desperate need of improvement.

RAUL: It’s about a lick of paint, it’s about letting micro businesses and small sme exist. So it's all about sustainability but what you're finding is that if we wait for government to do their bit, I don't think we'll ever get there - certainly not in the medium and short term.

SIVAN: I think time is running out. People are losing faith. We are seeing it with our investors. We're seeing it with our funders. // Let's not let it get to a state where it's now a no hope and people are now abandoning it .

VO: With a steady exodus of big corporates from the inner city - some feel that Ellis Park’s days are numbered and a relocation should be considered.

KEN: It's a big move.//we saw it with the Stormers in Western Province and the beloved Newlands Stadium. // I think maybe they should see it as an opportunity. They seriously need to consider the long term future.

VO: But that could be even more detrimental for the city.

Ellis Park is still a money spinner for the local economy - bringing in hundreds of million Rands. In 2022, the Bok - All Black test, at the stadium generated R630 million’s worth of revenue across the province - that just from a single game.

SIFISO: If now you're taking the last thing that we have that actually brings the revenue in the inner city, then how are our people supposed to make it? //if we don't bring people to entertainment, there's no way we can bring people again in the inner city.

PIETER: To fix something that is broken, it’s SOUTH African trait. Our resilience isn't it. I think there's still too much opportunity and still too much life left in that very iconic facility like this to just give up.

VISUALS Open on CCTV footage (3 seconds)

VO: Crime and decaying infrastructure. Joburgs inner city is in decline

KEN: If you look at the surrounding area around Ellis Park have there been any improvements in that area? // No, it doesn't look like it.

VO: But is the grime threatening the future of South African Rugby’s most famous stadium

PROMO 2 - 21 seconds
VISUALS Dirty inner city - three seconds AUDIO NOTE ** hard music

VO: This is the city of gold…

SIVAN: People are losing faith. You Can't invest in an environment that's deteriorating.

VO: Once a thriving metropolis, Johannesburg is in decline, and it’s threatening the future of its most iconic stadium.

PROMO 3 - 21 seconds
VISUALS - beautiful sexy Ellis Park - 3 seconds

VO: Ellis Park Stadium (pause) … one of South Africa’s most iconic landmarks

KEN: // the actual In-Stadium experience is fine. // that's in their control. But where they're situated, // Jo'burg CBD //`what, what can they do.

VO: Set in Johannesburgs decaying inner city… is the future of this arena under threat?

(BEAT) Sections in the area will remain closed for months to come - adding to the city’s already long list of challenges from water supply to road infrastructure and a general lack of municipal services SIVAN: This is a 20 year problem that's just now become too much to handle for the current coalition players.// what's happening is investors are moving away from the inner city. // they want to go to the environments that are controlled, where they have operational city improvement districts, where people pay levies to maintain the upkeep of the area. VO: Some feel, that’s exactly what Ellis Park Stadium should be doing. KEN: // if you look at the surrounding area around Ellis Park // is there anything going on there that makes you think, okay, things are improving, that if we just hold out, you know, there's a plan and things are going to get better? No, it doesn't look like it. VISUAL MOMENT VISUAL MUSIC SUNSET….. LINK: When you leave Ellis Park after a match, you leaving in the dark and you leaving a safe cocoon and you're entering a whole other world that, frankly, is scary. It's dark, it's grimy and has seedy elements. Has anything ever happened to me in the streets leaving the stadium? No. But do I feel uncomfortable and uneasy? Absolutely. DE KLERK: Your personal space gets smaller because you can’t see the people beyond the car. On the car. Each moment somebody is knocking on a window. We had quite a few incidents through here and it doesn't get reported the Hillbrow Police Station, the guy will drive home //he doesn't want to go to your police station because of the bad experience. CLAIRE: I mean, we're not even that far from here. We're not even that far from Ellis Park. It's just behind us. DE KLERK: This is a kilometer out of Ellis Park. //We have our strip clubs, quite big taverns, // and all this is aspects that's bringing the area down. VO: It seems that's affecting the game day experience, and could be the reason for the empty seats at the July test between the Boks and Argentina UPSOUND ETSEBETH SCORING… and Etsebeth… WHISTLE… VO: The more than 60 thousand seat stadium was anything but full. But, organisers were quick to point out the attendance was still a record for a game against the South Americans. But that hasn't spared the stadium from flak UPSOUND PIETER INTRO: Pieter Burger, Managing Director - EAP. PIETER: crime is a national problem within southern Africa that we're faced with and we need to deal with. And we tried to manage that through various different initiatives as best we possibly can. // over a thousand safety and security officers were deployed on the day that was just private security company // over 200 300 to JMPD and also SAPS officers // DE KLERK: The security companies does awesome jobs. JMPD are all on duty during the day, but my concern is the bigger picture. What is the city of Joburg doing to develop the area permanently? SIFISO: look ack - ignore it all you want it’s still parf of us need to embrace it. VO: But Small business owners are stepping up - it’s not all doom and gloom - INTRO RAUL: Raul de Lima, proprietor and owner of The Troyville Hotel RAUL: // it's up to us to do it,// It's about taking back and owning the city VO: Less than a kilometer from the stadium grounds is yet another iconic Joburg Landmark. The Troyville Hotel opened its doors in 1939 - the same year the Second World War began. A lot has happened in those 85 years, and owners have come and gone. RAUL: This is a kind of a property that sits sort of almost on the cusp of the wrong side of town, so to speak. // this building, this precinct. // It's iconic. VO: De Lima bought the Hotel two years ago, taking over what he calls a pretty run down gem and returning it to its former glory RAUL: what we really enjoyed was the fact that we could come here, put our money where our mouth was, invest, fix it up, create employment, // I think the community recognizes that we've invested and they respect that. SIFISO: A lot of change that needs to happen - let’s work together and turn our city back. VO: DE LIMA hopes his investment will draw other like-minded entrepreneurs back to areas in desperate need of improvement. RAUL: It’s about a lick of paint, it’s about letting micro businesses and small sme exist. So it's all about sustainability but what you're finding is that if we wait for government to do their bit, I don't think we'll ever get there - certainly not in the medium and short term. SIVAN: I think time is running out. People are losing faith. We are seeing it with our investors. We're seeing it with our funders. // Let's not let it get to a state where it's now a no hope and people are now abandoning it . VO: With a steady exodus of big corporates from the inner city - some feel that Ellis Park’s days are numbered and a relocation should be considered. KEN: It's a big move.//we saw it with the Stormers in Western Province and the beloved Newlands Stadium. // I think maybe they should see it as an opportunity. They seriously need to consider the long term future. VO: But that could be even more detrimental for the city. Ellis Park is still a money spinner for the local economy - bringing in hundreds of million Rands. In 2022, the Bok - All Black test, at the stadium generated R630 million’s worth of revenue across the province - that just from a single game. SIFISO: If now you're taking the last thing that we have that actually brings the revenue in the inner city, then how are our people supposed to make it? //if we don't bring people to entertainment, there's no way we can bring people again in the inner city. PIETER: To fix something that is broken, it’s SOUTH African trait. Our resilience isn't it. I think there's still too much opportunity and still too much life left in that very iconic facility like this to just give up. VO: But is the grime threatening the future of South African Rugby’s most famous stadium PROMO 2 - 21 seconds VISUALS Dirty inner city - three seconds AUDIO NOTE ** hard music VO: This is the city of gold… SIVAN: People are losing faith. You Can't invest in an environment that's deteriorating. VO: Once a thriving metropolis, Johannesburg is in decline, and it’s threatening the future of its most iconic stadium. PROMO 3 - 21 seconds VISUALS - beautiful sexy Ellis Park - 3 seconds VO: Ellis Park Stadium (pause) … one of South Africa’s most iconic landmarks KEN: // the actual In-Stadium experience is fine. // that's in their control. metadata.Summary: The Springboks’ final game on home ground raised questions about the future of the iconic Ellis Park Stadium – has it reached its sell-by date with Joburg CBD’s urban decay keeping spectators away? It allows us to have a look at the current state of the inner city – how did we get here, and what is the future for an area once the epicenter of business and play. We hit the streets, speak to some key players and address the challenges plaguing downtown Joburg.
metadata.Further information: We take a look at the history of Ellis Park and where it finds itself in 2023 – an epic stadium now plagued by inner city decay. We ask what the future holds for sporting events and businesses in the area that seems to be losing the battle to regenerate the Joburg CBD. **CAPACITY AT EVENTS – DROPPED. Over the last year there’s been a significant drop in attendance at sporting events held at Ellis Park – some have sighted the fall of the city and the security risks around the stadium. Speaking to Ken Borland from the Citizen – he agrees the area is not what it used to be but pointed out that there were factors to consider around the Springbok vs Agentine game – 1. Just two weeks earlier there was the Wallaby game at Loftus – a bigger competitor for the Boks from a spectator perspective and it was two big matches in GP in a short time and international tickets are cheap. 2. The weather – it was COLD in Jozi that Saturday. **ALTERNATIVE PROPERTY PERSPECTIVE The inner city may be in a shocking state for middle-class South Africans, but for foreigners and locals from rural communities downtown JHB is a step up, as sad as that may be – it is seen as a stepping stone to a better life for many who come from informal settlements and find a space in a big city to pursue jobs and a future for their families. **PROPERTY INTERVIEW TUHF is a specialised commercial property financing company that finances property investors exclusively in inner cities. This company has unique hands on insight into the challenges investors face when it comes to regenerating inner cities – they speak to the vision, the struggles with lack of service delivery and a surge in criminal activity. While there is interest from investors, and there has been some success to turn inner city precincts around (usually without government assistance) – it’s become increasingly challenging to keep their strategies going as Joburg seems to be crumbling. Many investors are now looking outside of downtown JHB to areas where there is more potential from privately managed services and less reliance on government. INTERVIEWS  THE STADIUM – Ellis Park Managing Director, Pieter Burger – we’ll film at the stadium. Do a walk through the museum, interview inside and maybe a bit outside on the streets around the stadium.  RUGBY LEGEND – TBC – I’m trying John Smit. Will hopefully know today. Otherwise, Ken Borland from the Citizen. The idea is to get a perspective from someone that has a special connection to the stadium but also sees the current state of the city as an issue – John Smit is also part of SSG, a security group.  LOCAL SECURITY – Hendrik de Klerk from Bad Boyz Security – we’ll film this late afternoon on our first shoot day, to get the rush hour effect, and to see the vibe change as the sun sets. We’ll also get visuals around the pipeline blast scene and get some links there.  BREACON OF HOPE - TROYVILLE HOTEL – they share their journey to keep their spot a must-visit location – what it takes to run a successful business in downtown Jozi and why they are still hopeful about the area.  INNER CITY PROPERTY GURU – Sivan Govender, Operations Director at TUHF ** I’m purposely avoiding the Municipality – they don’t know their arse from their elbow and the mayor keeps changing, and they bicker – the reality is it’s shitshow, they’re not doing anything and they’re just going to give us a bullshit take on it. TREATMENT  FILMING STYLE – I’m going to try and do a lot of it looser – outside, walk and talk, show and tell. Some will be in doors of course, but it’s a story about the city – I think we need to be in the city.  EDIT IDEAS – We won’t have vox pops with spectators – but will have some tweets and comments from Social Media so I’m thinking to build something device to bring up some of the comments. Working on a intro concept for the elements.
